page: Microsoft Azure D64_v5 is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 64 virtual CPUs and 256 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources are powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, comprising 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction flags such as AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance operates under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization with dedicated CPU core allocation.

The D64_v5 does not include local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on remote storage volumes for persistent data. This architectural profile directs its cost efficiency toward high compute density and system memory rather than bundled storage hardware. With no attached GPU, large language model generation drops significantly on heavier models, recording 2.61 tokens per second on 70B parameter architectures. Conversely, single-core benchmarks remain within average ranges across Geekbench and stress-ng tests.

Multi-core and throughput-focused benchmarks highlight the primary strengths of this instance. The D64_v5 achieves strong results in multi-threaded workloads, including 62,145.09 on multi-core stress-ng tests and 16,499.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate strong uncached read and write throughput at 294.62 GB/sec and 135.63 GB/sec, respectively. These characteristics translate to strong handling of concurrent data, evidenced by 62.27 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, 54.31 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and high scores in Clang software compilation.

Given its balanced CPU and memory footprint combined with strong multi-threaded scaling, the D64_v5 is suited for enterprise software builds, multi-threaded batch compilation, in-memory caching systems, distributed relational or document database engines, and high-traffic static web application tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure D64_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 256 GB of system RAM. Utilizing dedicated CPU allocations and hyper-threading under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 4.0 GB of memory per core and incorporates 48 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 vector support. The instance does not feature local storage disks or GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations. Benchmark results show average single-thread performance paired with strong multi-core compute capability, high uncached memory throughput, and robust network data handling. Demonstrating strong throughput in compilation, database operations, and Redis caching benchmarks, the D64_v5 is well suited for demanding general-purpose workloads, including high-concurrency web tiers, relational databases, continuous integration build clusters, and in-memory caches.
